After the eclipse prayer the Prophet said people will be tried in their graves, where the believer affirms Muhammad brought clear signs and the hypocrite says he does not know.

Earlier nations were ruined by questions and differences over their prophets; the Prophet disliked needless questions, feared night prayer becoming obligatory and grew angry when pressed; overburdening oneself is forbidden.
When some Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit, he waited for revelation, then recited that knowledge of the spirit is with his Lord.
People followed the Prophet in wearing and discarding gold rings, he forbade continuous fasting, Ali's scroll cursed innovators in Medina, and the Prophet rebuked those avoiding what he himself did.
Abu Bakr and Umar raised their voices before the Prophet over appointing a chief for Bani Tamim, the verse forbidding raised voices came down, and Umar spoke to him softly.
In his fatal illness the Prophet insisted Abu Bakr lead the prayer despite Aisha and Hafsa urging Umar, likening them to the companions of Joseph.
Uwaimir asked whether a husband who kills a man found with his wife is killed; the Prophet disliked the question, revelation came, they performed li'an, and he divorced her.
Ali and Abbas disputed the Bani Nadir property before Umar, who said the Prophet's property is not inherited but charity, and must be managed as he and Abu Bakr did.
Medina is a sanctuary whose trees may not be cut, and whoever innovates a heresy or sins there incurs the curse of Allah, the angels and all people.
Knowledge will vanish with the death of scholars, leaving the ignorant to give misleading verdicts by opinion, and at Siffin Sahl bin Hunaif told people to distrust their own opinions.
When the sick Jabir, revived by the Prophet's ablution water, asked how to deal with his wealth, the Prophet gave no reply until the verse of inheritance was revealed.
A woman asked for a day of teaching for women; the Prophet taught them, then said a woman who loses three children, or even two, is screened from the Fire.
A group of the Prophet's followers will stay victorious until Allah's order comes, understanding of the Quran and Sunna is Allah's favour, and the nation will remain good until then.
As verse 6:65 came down, the Prophet sought refuge with Allah's Face from punishment from above and below, and called party strife and mutual violence the easier warnings.
To a bedouin who doubted his black son was his, the Prophet pointed to grey camels among red ones, colour inherited from ancestors, and did not let him deny paternity.
Told of a mother who vowed Hajj but died, the Prophet bade her daughter perform it for her, as she would pay her debts, for Allah has more right.
One may wish to be like only two: a man given wealth who spends it rightly, and a man given religious wisdom who judges by it and teaches it.
For a woman miscarrying from a blow, the blood money is a male or female slave, as Al-Mughira told Umar, who demanded a witness and got Muhammad bin Maslama.
The Prophet's followers will copy earlier nations span by span, even into a mastigure's hole; asked if these were Persians and Byzantines, or Jews and Christians, he said who else.
Adam's first son shares the burden of every unjust killing, for he was the first to establish murder.
A bedouin refused release from his pledge left Medina, which expels impurities like bellows, and Umar delayed a sermon until Medina, place of the Sunna and the companions.
Wiping his nose on linen, Abu Huraira recalled fainting from hunger between the Prophet's pulpit and Aisha's dwelling, where passers-by thought him mad.
Ibn Abbas, though young, attended the Eid prayer with the Prophet, who prayed and preached, then bade the women give alms, which Bilal collected.
The Prophet used to go to the Quba mosque, sometimes walking and sometimes riding.
Aisha asked to be buried with the Prophet's wives rather than beside him, lest she be thought sanctified, yet let Umar be buried with his two companions.
The Prophet prayed Asr early enough that one could reach Al-Awali, three or four miles away, while the sun was still high.
The Sa' measure in the Prophet's time equalled a Mudd and a third of a later Mudd, and he asked Allah to bless the measures of Medina's people.
The Jews brought a man and a woman who had committed illegal sexual intercourse, and the Prophet had them stoned near the mosque where biers were placed.
The Prophet said Uhud loves us and is loved by us, made Medina a sanctuary as Abraham did Mecca, and between his house and pulpit is a garden of Paradise.
The Prophet held horse races, conditioned horses running from Al-Hafya to Thaniyat-al-Wada and others from there to the mosque of Bani Zuraiq.
Umar and Uthman were heard preaching from the Prophet's pulpit.
Aisha and the Prophet bathed together, taking water from one large copper vessel.
The Prophet made an alliance between the Ansar and Quraish in Anas's house in Medina, and invoked Allah against Bani Sulaim in prayer for a month.
The Prophet allied the Ansar and Quraish in Anas's house at Medina; Abdullah bin Salam let a visitor drink from the Prophet's bowl and pray in his mosque.
The Prophet was told to pray in the blessed Aqiq valley and declare Umra and Hajj, fixed the miqats, and dreamt at Dhul-Hulaifa he was in a blessed valley.
Rising from bowing in the morning prayer the Prophet praised Allah, and in the last rak'a asked Him to curse certain people; Allah revealed that the decision is not his.
Asked at night whether he and Fatima would pray, Ali said their souls are in Allah's Hands; the Prophet left striking his thigh, saying man is most quarrelsome.
At Bait al-Midras the Prophet called the Jews thrice to embrace Islam and be safe, then said he wanted to exile them and they should sell their property.
On Resurrection Noah's people will deny he conveyed Allah's message, and Muhammad's followers will testify for him; the Prophet recited the verse making them a just nation of witnesses.
The Prophet told his Khaibar governor not to take one sa' of good dates for two of mixed, but to exchange equal measures or sell and buy with the price.
